To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the V3 loop quasispecies of the HIV-1-infested long-term-nonprogressor mother and child pair showed no evidence of phenotypic changes in the V3 loop region, and the high genetic diversity of HIV-1 strains in this HIV-1 infected long-term-nonprogressive mother and child pair is directly proportional to the immunocompetent status of the mother and child.

there was a predominance in lower V3 loop charges, and there was an absence of critical changes in the V3 loop region of the HIV-1 envelope that are critical in determining phenotypic tropism during the HIV-1 infection of the mother-child pair.

a high intrahost genetic heterogeneity in the V3 region of human immunodeficy virus type 1 strains from the first mother-child pair of HIV-1-inflected long-term-nonprogressors may have been a critical factor for their survival with stable CD4 cell counts for over 13 years.

the identification and characterization of the HIV-1 quasispecies in the first HIV- 1-infected mother-child pair who have survived for > 13 years with stable immunocompetent CD4 T cell numbers.

the molecular analyses of HIV-1 strains derived from plasma and the peripheral blood mononucleated cells of the first mother and child pair who have survived for more than 13 years with stable immunocompetence.
the molecular characterization of the V3 loop quasispecies of HIV-1 strains derived from the plasma and peripheral blood cells of the first mother-child HIV-1-infested pair.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HIV-1 V3 loop of the first long- term-nonprogressing mother (mother) and child (child) pair is not the sole determinant of HIV-1 disease progression.

the genetic diversity between HIV strains from this HIV-infected long-term nonprogressing mother-child HIV-1-infested long-term-nonprogression pair was directly proportional and correlated with their immunocompetence and survival.
the HIV-1 V3 loop quasispecies from this HIV- 1-infected longterm-nonprogressing motherchild pair are not phenotypically neutralized.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the V3 region genetic diversity in HIV-1-infested cells from this HIV- 1-infected longterm-nonprogressing mother- child pair was directly related to the duration of immunocompetence.
a high genetic diversity of HIV-1 strains is directly proportional to the immunocompetence of the host.

the HIV-1-inflected long-term-nonprogressor mother and child pair have survived for more than 13 years with a stable CD4 T-cell counts due to the presence of a high genetic diversity in HIV-1 V3 region and absence of the critical genotypic changes for phenotypic tropism.

a high genetic diversity of HIV-1 strains in the first long-term HIV-1-inflicted mother-child pair is directly proportional to their immunocompetence.
the HIV-1 strains in this HIV-1 mother-child pair have evolved to a state where they are not as virulent and are less able to cause disease.
